deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page sits in Riemann's 'Gravitation und Licht' fragment (Naturphilosophie, 1853). In the published Werke, Blatt 10 and 11 are printed under 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'.

PART 1: end of section e (carried over from p.15). The previous page states a variational principle. Write eta = (eta_1, eta_2, eta_3)(x,t) for the displacement of the space-filling 'Stoff', V(x,t) for a scalar, and dm for the gravitating elements of ponderable bodies with trajectories x(t). The action is

S = 1/2 ∫ [ |∂_t eta|^2 - c^2 |curl eta|^2 ] d^3x dt + ∫ V ( div ∂_t eta d^3x + 4π dm ) dt + 2π ∫ dm |dx/dt|^2 dt.

The requirement is that every admissible variation produces only a second-order change in S, i.e. δS = 0. This page concludes that then v = ∂eta/∂t is the velocity of the Stoff motion and V is the potential at time t at the point (x_1, x_2, x_3).

My reconstruction of the Euler–Lagrange equations, writing dm = ρ d^3x:
(a) Varying V gives div v = ∂_t div eta = -4πρ. In empty space this is equation I of p.15, div v = 0.
(b) Varying eta, after integrating the V-term by parts in x and t, gives ∂_t^2 eta + c^2 curl curl eta = ∂_t ∇V.
  - Taking the curl gives (∂_t^2 - c^2 Δ) curl eta = 0. Differentiating in t gives (∂_t^2 - c^2 Δ) curl v = 0, which is system II of p.15.
  - Equivalently, (∂_t^2 - c^2 Δ) v - ∂_t^2 ∇V is a gradient. This matches the pencil note dW = d ∂_t^2 V.
(c) Varying the trajectory x(t) of each element: the kinetic term 2π dm |ẋ|^2 gives -4π dm ẍ, and the coupling 4π V(x(t)) dm gives 4π dm ∇V. Hence ẍ = ∇V, every ponderable element accelerating with the gradient of V.
(d) Splitting v = ∇V + w with div w = 0 (as on p.15), (a) gives ΔV = -4πρ. So V = ∫ dm/r, the Newtonian (Gauss-sign) potential, and ẍ = ∇V is Newtonian attraction. This justifies the sentence on this page.

PART 2: Blatt 10. Riemann axiomatises the Newtonian explanation of falling bodies and planetary motion as four 'causes'.
1. There is infinite Euclidean space, and ponderable bodies change place only continuously.
2. Each ponderable point has at each instant a cause of definite magnitude and direction (its state of motion), measured by its velocity. He remarks that these phenomena do not yet require different (inertial) masses.
3. At each point of space there is an accelerating force a(x,t), the same for every ponderable point located there, which adds vectorially to the existing motion: ẍ = a(x,t).
4. Each ponderable point j carries an absolute gravity m_j generating the field a(x) = -Σ_j m_j (x - x_j)/|x - x_j|^3, with superposition. The inverse-square law is (me) a = ∇ Σ m_j/|x - x_j|.

He then announces his programme: identify the accelerating gravity at each point of space with the motion of a homogeneous substance continuously filling all of space. The next page adds that the flow velocity is parallel and proportional to the force. This is the ether-flow (sink) model of gravitation that section e encodes variationally.
errors: Notational slips on p.15: '∂η/∂x∂t' must mean the mixed derivative ∂^2 η_ι/∂x_ι∂t summed over ι, and the final '∂t' should be 'dt'.
The claim 'v = velocity, V = potential' follows only together with the decomposition v = ∇V + w and suitable boundary/decay conditions, which are left implicit ('unter geeigneten Grenzbedingungen').
The identification of V with ∫dm/r also needs V to vanish at infinity, which is not stated.
With the coefficients 2π and 4π the signs are consistent with ΔV = -4πρ and ẍ = ∇V.
In 4, the gravitational constant is absorbed into the 'absolute Schwerkraft'; this is fine as stated.

results.what: Single action functional (field Lagrangian for a transverse elastic ether with wave speed c, Lagrange-multiplier coupling to point masses via V, and particle kinetic term) whose stationarity yields Newtonian gravity plus wave equations for curl v
results.modern_name: Variational (Lagrangian) field theory of gravitation/ether coupled to matter; Lagrange-multiplier constraint div v = -4πρ
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1853 (published posthumously in Werke 1876, 'Gravitation und Licht'); related ether models of gravity by Challis, Bjerknes, Kelvin

results.what: Axiomatisation of Newtonian gravity into four 'causes', with the remark that inertial mass differences are not needed (universality of free fall)
results.modern_name: Field formulation of Newtonian gravity; universality of free fall (weak equivalence principle)

results.what: Programme to explain gravity by the motion of a space-filling homogeneous substance whose velocity is proportional to the gravitational force
results.usually_credited_to: Various 19th-c. authors; Riemann's version known from Werke

deep.surprise_reason: This text is Riemann's 'Gravitation und Licht' / 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' material, printed in his Gesammelte Werke and well studied. Nothing here is new relative to the published record.

checkable.asserts: Equals 0: the potential V = m/r is harmonic away from the mass, consistent with div v = 0 in empty space.
Equals 0: |grad(1/r)| = 1/r^2, the inverse-square accelerating force of assumption 4.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.vector import CoordSys3D, curl, divergence, gradient; N=CoordSys3D('N'); f=Function('f')(N.x,N.y,N.z); simplify(curl(gradient(f)))
checkable.asserts: Equals the zero vector: the gradient part u = ∇V drops out of curl v, so only the transverse part w obeys the wave equation II.

checkable.sympy: F=[Function('F%d'%i)(N.x,N.y,N.z) for i in range(3)]; A=F[0]*N.i+F[1]*N.j+F[2]*N.k; simplify(curl(curl(A)) - (gradient(divergence(A)) - (diff(F[0],N.x,2)+diff(F[0],N.y,2)+diff(F[0],N.z,2))*N.i - (diff(F[1],N.x,2)+diff(F[1],N.y,2)+diff(F[1],N.z,2))*N.j - (diff(F[2],N.x,2)+diff(F[2],N.y,2)+diff(F[2],N.z,2))*N.k))
checkable.asserts: Equals 0: curl curl A = grad div A - ΔA. This identity turns the Euler-Lagrange equation η_tt + c^2 curl curl η = ∂_t ∇V into (∂_t^2 - c^2 Δ) curl η = 0.
Gives 4π V'(X) - 4π X'' = 0, i.e. ẍ = ∇V: the trajectory variation of the dm-terms yields Newtonian motion in the potential V (one-dimensional check).

transcription_corrections: Line 'Alsdann sind die Größen ∂η/∂t (=v, d.h.)': the manuscript writes dη/dt, to be read as ∂η_ι/∂t (components).

Otherwise the transcription agrees with the image. '((Blatt 10))' is an editorial marker, and the numbered items 1, 2), 3, 4, are faithfully reproduced, including the inconsistent punctuation after the numbers.
